execution_method: local original-resolution visual inspection against the versioned judge rubric
pass_rule: All required directional relations must hold; near-zero means <= 0.02, high means >= 0.70, and an order effect is material when any compared component differs by more than 0.05.

cases.expected_relation: Candidate is pixel-identical to Style truth; style, color, composition, and technical loss must be near zero.
evidence: Candidate and Style truth are the same local PNG, so the transferable poster layout, palette, contours, texture, and technical detail are visually identical.
The candidate depicts the non-transferable style-reference woman rather than the supplied man, which explains the identity and semantic losses and is not part of this style self-match relation.

cases.expected_relation: Candidate is pixel-identical to Person truth; identity and semantic identity-subject loss must be near zero.
evidence: Candidate and Person truth are the same local PNG, so the face, skin tone, haircut, gaze, expression, and pose are identical.
The candidate is an unstyled neutral-background photograph, not the requested editorial poster; the high style, color, and composition losses are expected and do not negate identity self-match.

cases.expected_relation: The unstyled person photograph retains low identity loss but has high style and color loss against the editorial illustration.
evidence: The candidate is exactly the person reference, preserving the same man’s visible face, hair, gaze, expression, and pose.
It is a pale neutral photographic close-up with no navy ink contours, cel-shading, coloured poster fields, abstract disks, rules, dry-brush marks, or printed-paper treatment.

cases.expected_relation: Changing only display order, while preserving image labels and roles, must not materially alter the assessment.
evidence: With labels preserved, the same photograph still exactly matches Person truth and still lacks every observed transferable editorial treatment from Style truth.
No component changed relative to the baseline cross-domain assessment.
